rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is sparse, so this experiment tests a multimodal configuration with pca_n2000 RNA encoder, resnet50 image encoder, transformer aggregation, and concat fusion. It clarifies the baseline performance of a balanced multimodal setup, which is critical for understanding if multimodal approaches outperform single-modal ones. This is the best use of the first experiment to establish initial performance benchmarks.

The existing evidence shows that the multimodal setup with pca_n2000 RNA encoder, resnet50 image encoder, and transformer aggregation (config_002) achieves 0.579 validation accuracy. This experiment tests changing the fusion method from concat to weighted, which could improve performance by allowing more nuanced interaction between modalities. It clarifies whether weighted fusion is better than simple concatenation in this context, leveraging the existing multimodal setup to exploit promising directions without overcomplicating the model.

Existing evidence shows that weighted fusion (config_019) slightly outperforms concat (config_002) in F1, but aggregation methods remain unexplored. This experiment tests avgpool aggregation with weighted fusion, a key design choice that could improve performance. It balances exploration of aggregation methods with exploitation of the promising weighted fusion approach.

The existing evidence shows that avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion (as in config_007) achieve the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests whether replacing the image encoder from resnet50 to imagenet_vit_l (a stronger vision transformer) while keeping aggregation and fusion unchanged could further improve performance. This clarifies the impact of the image encoder choice on accuracy, a critical design decision with weak prior evidence.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with pca_n2000 RNA encoder and weighted fusion (config_007) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.639). This experiment tests using the more advanced imagenet_vit_l image encoder with transformer aggregation (instead of avgpool) while retaining weighted fusion. This clarifies whether the image encoder's quality or aggregation method has a greater impact on performance, balancing exploration of key design choices with building on the current top-performing configuration.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, PCA RNA, ViT-L image, AvgPool aggregation, and Weighted fusion (config_022) achieve 0.635 accuracy. This experiment tests ScVI_n200 RNA with ViT-L image and same aggregation/fusion to clarify if RNA encoder choice (PCA vs ScVI) impacts performance. It balances exploitation of high-performing components (ViT-L, AvgPool, Weighted) with exploration of RNA encoder alternatives, targeting the most impactful design choice.

The existing evidence shows config_046 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l with avgpool and weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.706). This experiment tests replacing avgpool with transformer aggregation while keeping other components the same, to determine if the aggregation method significantly impacts performance. It's a logical extension of the top-performing configuration, balancing exploitation of promising components with exploration of alternative aggregation strategies.

The existing evidence shows config_006 (0.724989 accuracy) is the best so far using scvi_n200 RNA and imagenet_vit_l image encoders with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion. This experiment tests the same RNA/image encoders but with avgpool aggregation and concat fusion, clarifying if the current best's performance is robust to changes in aggregation/fusion methods. It directly addresses uncertainty about whether these choices are optimal, balancing exploitation of the top-performing setup with exploration of alternative configurations.

The existing evidence shows that configurations using scvi_n200 RNA encoder and weighted fusion (e.g., config_006) achieve high accuracy (0.725). This experiment tests using resnet50 image encoder and concat fusion, which could clarify if switching image encoders or fusion methods further improves performance. It balances exploration of key design choices (encoder/fusion) while building on the strong foundation of scvi_n200.

The existing evidence shows that configurations using scvi_n200 RNA encoder and imagenet_vit_l image encoder with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (e.g., config_006) achieve high accuracy (0.724989). This experiment tests a similar setup but with scgpt RNA encoder and resnet50 image encoder, which could potentially improve performance by leveraging different encoder strengths. It clarifies whether alternative encoders maintain high accuracy, balancing exploration of encoder choices with exploitation of proven aggregation/fusion strategies.
